lead.headline: SUPREME COURT ORDERS RED WARNINGS ON HIGH-SUGAR, SALT & FAT FOODS
lead.deck: The FSSAI has four months to frame prominent front-of-pack warnings, with a separate red symbol for each nutrient of concern.
paragraphs: The Supreme Court directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to prepare a single-phase warning-label regime for packaged foods high in total sugar, saturated fat or salt. Each nutrient must have its own prominent red hexagon and pictogram.

The court ordered the regulator to revisit its thresholds and finalise draft rules in about four months. Manufacturers would then have a year-long transition to comply; the bench said delays in informing consumers carried public-health costs, particularly for children.

image.alt: Supreme Court of India, in a report on the court's directions for packaged-food warning labels.
image.caption: The court linked clear food labels to health and informed consumer choice. Photo: PTI / Hindustan Times.

sidebarStory.headline: BENGALURU AIRPORT SET TO INTRODUCE SIMULTANEOUS RUNWAY OPERATIONS
sidebarStory.subhead: The new arrangement could raise approved capacity from about 60 to 85 aircraft movements an hour.
paragraphs: Kempegowda International Airport has completed trials of simultaneous departures from its north and south runways. The airport is expected to introduce the more flexible operating arrangement on November 27; the Union civil aviation minister was reported likely to visit for a formal launch.
DGCA approval came on November 3. The change could lift capacity by about 42%, though actual delays will still depend on weather, traffic and air-traffic-control clearances.

image.alt: Illustration of simultaneous runway departures at Bengaluru airport.
image.caption: Bengaluru airport's trials recorded departures from both runways. Image: Moneycontrol.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru civic services, infrastructure and jobs news

stories.headline: GBA BEGINS SENDING FREE E-KHATAS TO 24 LAKH OWNERS ON WHATSAPP
paragraphs: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has begun distributing property e-Khatas as PDF files through WhatsApp under the state’s Bhu-Guarantee programme.
The rollout is intended to reach around 24 lakh property owners. Residents should use the official GBA channel and check their document details; the service is described as free.

stories.headline: EJIPURA FLYOVER MAY MISS EARLY-2027 OPENING AS LAND DELAYS PERSIST
paragraphs: The 2.38-km Ejipura flyover, begun in 2017 and originally due in 2019, may not be ready even by early 2027 as pending land acquisition continues to hold up work.
Officials say the project is about 82% complete and are targeting the right-side stretch by December. Commuters continue to face congestion around the unfinished corridor.

image.alt: A man at the unfinished Ejipura flyover construction site in Bengaluru.
image.caption: The long-delayed flyover remains affected by pending land acquisition. Photo: The Indian Express.

stories.headline: SIT NAMES IAS OFFICER, MIDDLEMAN IN FIRST KPSC RECRUITMENT-SCAM CHARGESHEET
paragraphs: The Karnataka Special Investigation Team filed its first chargesheet in an alleged KPSC veterinary-doctor recruitment scam, naming former exams controller Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar and middleman Basavaraj Kannale.
Investigators allege exam questions were leaked to 10 candidates for bribes totalling ₹1.52 crore. The chargesheet cites 155 witnesses; the allegations have yet to be tested at trial.

image.alt: File photograph accompanying the report on the KPSC recruitment investigation.
image.caption: The chargesheet names former KPSC exams controller Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar. File photo: The Indian Express.

groups.ariaLabel: India court, Parliament and education news

stories.headline: SC QUASHES ANAND MOHAN'S EARLY RELEASE, ORDERS HIM TO SURRENDER WITHIN A MONTH
paragraphs: The Supreme Court set aside the Bihar government’s 2023 remission order for former MP Anand Mohan, who was serving a life sentence in the 1994 murder of Gopalganj district magistrate G Krishnaiah.

The bench also struck down the prison-manual amendment that enabled the release and directed Mohan to surrender within a month. Bihar may begin a fresh remission process only after he returns to custody.

stories.headline: PARLIAMENT TO RECONVENE ON NOVEMBER 30 FOR ESSENTIAL BUSINESS
paragraphs: The government has asked the presiding officers of both Houses to resume Parliament on Monday, November 30, for a brief sitting to transact essential government business, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said.
The government asked the presiding officers to resume proceedings for a brief sitting to transact essential business. A detailed agenda had not been announced in the report.

stories.headline: CBSE STUDENTS CAN KEEP THEIR CURRENT TWO- OR THREE-LANGUAGE CHOICES THIS YEAR: SC
paragraphs: The Supreme Court clarified the transition rules for CBSE’s three-language policy: students already taking three languages may continue with those choices, while students taking two may keep that combination for this academic year.
Those continuing with two languages are expected to add a third next year. The clarification is meant to prevent students in Classes 6–9 from having to change their language combinations mid-year.

groups.ariaLabel: India agriculture, industry and environment news

stories.headline: INDIA POSTS RECORD 378.54 MILLION TONNES OF FOODGRAINS IN 2025–26
paragraphs: Final estimates released by the Agriculture Ministry put foodgrain production at a record 378.54 million tonnes in 2025–26, up 20.81 million tonnes from the previous year.
The first estimate for the current kharif season is 167.14 million tonnes, above the five-year average despite delayed monsoon rains and soil-moisture stress in several states, including Karnataka.

stories.headline: CABINET CLEARS ₹11,000-CRORE SCHEME TO BOOST CONSTRUCTION-EQUIPMENT MAKING
paragraphs: The Union Cabinet approved an ₹11,000-crore scheme to expand domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment, part of a wider set of approvals totalling ₹19,934 crore.
The programme is intended to build local capacity and suppliers in a sector that relies on imported equipment and components. The government announced the approval on November 25.

stories.headline: WAYANAD SET TO BE DECLARED INDIA'S FIRST E-WASTE-FREE DISTRICT
paragraphs: Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan is scheduled to formally declare Wayanad India’s first completely e-waste-free district at an event in Kalpetta today.

A three-month campaign collected discarded electronics from homes, offices, schools and public places for scientific processing. The district says continued collection and monitoring will be needed to sustain the status.

groups.ariaLabel: Indian cue sports, tennis and hockey news

stories.headline: PANKAJ ADVANI BECOMES FIRST INDIAN TO WIN THE CRUCIBLE CUP
paragraphs: Bengaluru-raised cue-sports champion Pankaj Advani swept Malta’s Tony Drago 6–0 in the final in Reading, England, to become the first Indian to win the Crucible Cup.
Advani beat former world champion Neil Robertson and Joe Perry en route to the title, dropping only three frames. India is set to host the next edition in 2027.

stories.headline: KYRGIOS, BUBLIK AND SVITOLINA TO HEADLINE BENGALURU TENNIS LEAGUE
paragraphs: Nick Kyrgios, Alexander Bublik, Elina Svitolina, Belinda Bencic and Karolina Pliskova are set to headline the four-day World Tennis League in Bengaluru from December 17.
The league stage runs through December 19, with the championship final scheduled for December 20. Four teams will compete for a place in the final.

stories.headline: HOCKEY INDIA LEAGUE SETS JANUARY RETURN; PLAYER AUCTION ON DECEMBER 7
paragraphs: Hockey India says the 2026–27 Hockey India League season will begin in the first week of January, with the men's and women's player auction scheduled for December 7 in New Delhi.
The season is set to feature six men's and four women's teams. Franchises enter the trading and retention phase before the auction, with player trades due by November 29.
